name: calls
title: Calls
summary: Video meetings with a shareable link and a lobby for guests, and instant calls that ring people's devices.

env.name: LIVEKIT_URL
env.doc: LiveKit server URL clients connect to (wss://<project>.livekit.cloud, or your self-hosted wss:// URL). Unset with the key and secret = call routes answer 503 calls_unconfigured. dev-up's calls hook runs a local server and fills it.
env.source: cloud.livekit.io → Project → Settings → Project URL, or your self-hosted server's public URL

env.name: LIVEKIT_API_KEY
env.doc: LiveKit API key: signs join tokens and server API calls, and is the issuer LiveKit's webhooks are checked against.
env.source: cloud.livekit.io → Project → Settings → Keys, or the keys: block of your livekit.yaml

env.name: LIVEKIT_API_SECRET
env.doc: LiveKit API secret for LIVEKIT_API_KEY (at least 32 characters outside development). Never sent to clients.
env.source: Shown once when the key is created in LiveKit Cloud; self-hosted: livekit-server generate-keys

env.name: LIVEKIT_API_URL
env.doc: http(s) origin the backend calls LiveKit's server API on, when it differs from LIVEKIT_URL (a private network address). Default: LIVEKIT_URL with https:// (http:// for ws://).

env.name: CALLS_TOKEN_TTL
env.doc: How long a join token is valid for connecting (Go duration, 1m–6h). LiveKit refreshes tokens for people already in a call.

env.name: CALLS_RING_TIMEOUT
env.doc: How long an instant call rings before it becomes a missed call (Go duration, 10s–5m).

env.name: CALLS_MAX_PARTICIPANTS
env.doc: Most people in one call (2–1000), enforced by the media server.

env.name: CALLS_LOCAL_LIVEKIT
env.doc: true: dev-up runs a local LiveKit server on 127.0.0.1 (ports +7 and +8 of the block) and points the backend at it, unless LIVEKIT_URL is set in .env.dev.

env.name: CALLS_LIVEKIT_DOWNLOAD
env.doc: true: when livekit-server isn't on PATH, dev-up fetches the pinned release into .data/bin (Linux: the release binary; macOS: builds the release source with Go, about 2 minutes once). Both are checksum-verified. false: install it yourself (brew install livekit).

stitch: Production media: create a LiveKit Cloud project (or self-host livekit-server), set LIVEKIT_URL (wss://), LIVEKIT_API_KEY and LIVEKIT_API_SECRET, and add the webhook <PUBLIC_API_URL>/webhooks/livekit in LiveKit (Cloud: Settings → Webhooks, signed with that key; self-hosted: webhook.urls + webhook.api_key in livekit.yaml). Without the webhook, attendance history stays empty.
Decide who may ring or invite whom: calls.SetCallPolicy (default: people who share an organization) and calls.SetDirectory for the people picker; add block checks there if the app has moderation.

Calendars and other features create meetings with calls.CreateMeeting(ctx, tx, calls.MeetingInput{…, Source: &calls.Source{Kind: "calendar.event", ID: eventID}}) inside their own transaction and send their own invitations (a 409 means the source already has an active meeting: create without one); update or cancel with calls.UpdateMeeting / calls.CancelMeeting, find it again with calls.MeetingBySource. On the client, setCallsScheduleAction (web and mobile, @/features/calls/seams) can send "Schedule a meeting" to the calendar's new-event link, and setCallsSourceLink (web and mobile) maps a meeting's source to the page that manages it ("Open in Calendar"); Calls never edits or cancels sourced meetings itself.

Time zones: calls.SetUserZone(fn) gives each person's zone (e.g. calendar.UserZone) so invitations, agent previews and search read in it; without it, invitations use the inviter's device zone (sent as time_zone) and always name the zone. On the client, call setCallsTimeZone(zone) (shared, web and mobile) from a session mount with the person's zone (e.g. their calendar settings' zone) so Calls shows times on the same clock; times in another zone than the device's are labelled.

Channels and DMs: a "Start call" button calls POST /v1/calls/calls {user_ids} (or calls.StartCall from Go) and opens /meet/<code>?autojoin=1. Keep the product words the same everywhere: Start call (an instant call), New meeting (a link), Video call (a calendar location type).
Set PUBLIC_WEB_URL: join links are PUBLIC_WEB_URL/meet/<code> (public on web: guests knock there). Mobile: configure universal links for /meet/* to open the app's meet/[code] route.

Privacy policy: name LiveKit (or your SFU host) as a processor of call audio and video; calls aren't recorded. Mobile: the plugin adds camera and microphone purpose strings and iOS background audio; rebuild the dev client.
Mobile placement: Calls is a Home row; give it a tab if calls are a primary destination.
